record.evidence_text: in microgravity, weight-bearing bones like the spine and hips don’t need to be as strong to support the human body. Consequently, on average, bones lose between 1% and 1.5% of their density each month during four-to-six-month missions.
This rate of bone loss can make crew members susceptible to fractures and to premature osteoporosis, a disease that weakens bones as people age.
